cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Hello? JAN: Oh hello. My name's Jan.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Are you the right person to talk to about the Buckworth Conservation Group?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: PETER: Yes, I'm Peter. I’m the secretary. JAN: Good.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: I’ve just moved to this area, and I’m interested in getting involved.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: I was in a similar group where I used to live.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Could you tell me something about your activities, please? PETER: Of course.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Well, we have a mixture of regular activities and special events.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: One of the regular ones is trying to keep the beach free of litter.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: A few of us spend a couple of hours a month on it, and it's awful how much there is to

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: clear. I wish people would be more responsible and take it home with them.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: JAN: totally agree. I'd be happy to help with that.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Is it OK to take dogs? PETER: I'm afraid not, as they're banned from the beach itself.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: You can take them along the cliffs, though. And children are welcome. JAN: Right.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: PETER: We also manage a nature reserve, and there's a lot to do there all year round.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: For example, because it's a popular place to visit, we spend a lot of time looking after

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: the paths and making sure they're in good condition for walking.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: JAN: could certainly help with that. PETER Good.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: And we have a programme of creating new habitats there.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: We've just finished making and installing nesting boxes for birds to use, and next we're

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: going to work on encouraging insects — they're important for the biodiversity of he

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: reserve.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: They certainly are.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: PETER: Oh, and we're also running a project to identify the different species of

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: butterflies hat visit the reserve. You might be interested in taking part in that.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: JAN: Sure.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I was involved in something similar where I used to live, counting all the species of

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: moths. I'd enjoy that.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: PETER Another job we're doing at the reserve is replacing the wall on the southern side,

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: between the parking area and our woodshed. It was badly damaged in a storm ast month.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: JAN: OK.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: PETER Then as I said, we have a programme of events as well, both at the weekend, and

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: during the week. JAN: Right. I presume you have guided walks?

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I'd like to get to know the local countryside, as lm new to the area.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Yes, we do. The next walk is to Ruston Island, a week on Saturday.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: We'll be meeting in the car park at Dunsmore Beach at low tide — that's when the sands

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: are dry enough for us to walk to the island without getting wet. JAN: Sounds good.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: The island's a great place to explore. It's quite small, and it's got a range of habitats.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: It's also an ideal location for seeing seals just off the coast, or even on the beach.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: JAN: OK. And is there anything we should bring, like a picnic, for instance?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: PETER: Yes, do bring one, as it's a full-day walk.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: And of course it'll be wet walking across and back, so make sure your boots are

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: waterproof. JAN: I must buy a new pair — there's a hole in one of my current ones!

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Well, I'd definitely like to come on the walk. PETER: Great.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Then later this month we're having a one-day woodwork session in Hopton Wood.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: JAN: I've never tried that before. Is it OK for beginners to take part? PETER: Definitely.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: There'll be a couple of experts leading the session, and we keep the number of

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: participants down, so you'll get as much help as you need. JAN: Excellent!

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: I'd love to be able to make chairs. PETER: That's probably too ambitious for one day!

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: You'll be starting with wooden spoons, and of course learning how to use the tools.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: And anything you make is yours to take home with you. JAN: That sounds like fun.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: When is it? PETER: It's on the 17th, from 10 a.m. until 3.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: There's a charge of £35, including lunch, or £40 if you want to camp in the wood.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: JAN: I should think I'll come home the same day.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Well, I'd certainly like to join the group. So, hello everyone.
